The failing assertion is useMfaEnrollment.test.tsx:321:57 — the round-3 expect(isStepUpRequiredError(result.current.error)).toBe(true) — and the pre-existing toBe('Sign in again with your authenticator before removing this factor.') at :320 PASSED. It now FAILS after 1 draw, counterexample [["RepWorth"]] — the round-3 line expect(taken.has(next)).toBe(false) at mfa.test.ts:218 is what closes it. A Markdown directory row has no covering test and cannot be mutated meaningfully; it is verified by hand-resolution under duty 3 instead. Result recorded there: `src/proxy.ts` `:260-271` resolves EXACTLY to `getAalGate` at HEAD (signature at :260, `getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel()` at :264, the lenient `nextLevel === 'aal2' && currentLevel !== 'aal2'` test at :268, closing brace at :271), so RT-1149-F4 is closed. `prevalidate-plan.py` was re-run and again reported "CITATIONS: 0 checked" on this file — its grammar does not read the bare "(`:260-271`, …)" form — so no part of this verdict rests on that script.

findings.title: Two independent copies of `/sign in again/i` with nothing binding them, and the new test asserted the exact copy string rather than the consumer’s predicate
findings.reason: FIXED, and the fix is exactly the behavioural replacement this finding proposed: the hook test now imports the real consumer predicate (useMfaEnrollment.test.tsx:26) and asserts isStepUpRequiredError is false on the hook's enrollment sentence (:278) and true on the unenroll-403 hint (:321). Measured, not read: r3-01 changes SecuritySections.tsx:42 from /sign in again/i to /verify again/i and the suite goes red at :321 ONLY — the pre-existing string assertion at :320 passes. So the two copies are now bound at the place they must agree, for a pattern CHANGE. The import is legal: eslint.config.mjs:253 and :251 ignore `**/__tests__/**` for the @/app leaf ban, and `npx eslint` over both changed test files exits 0 at HEAD. What the binding does NOT catch is a widening that adds an alternative; that residue is opened as RT-1149-F6 rather than left inside a closed finding.

findings.title: The new predicate binding is directional — it catches a CHANGE to the presentation pattern but not a WIDENING that adds an alternative, which is the drift scenario RT-1149-F3 originally described
findings.reason: Static, and exact — no launch was spent on it deliberately (see below). Both new assertions run isStepUpRequiredError over two FIXED literals: 'Could not start MFA enrollment.' (:278) and 'Sign in again with your authenticator before removing this factor.' (:321). A mutation of SecuritySections.tsx:42 that only ADDS an alternative — /sign in again|re-authenticate/i, the literal example RT-1149-F3 used — classifies both literals exactly as before, so both assertions still pass and the repository stays green; meanwhile a provider message containing 're-authenticate' slips the hook's local /sign in again/i guard at useMfaEnrollment.ts:84 and re-acquires RT-1149-F2's defect. Why no mutation row: such a mutant would survive on a branch these two literals provably never execute, which the skill classifies `inconclusive` (class oracle) by construction and which would force INCOMPLETE_ORACLE while carrying zero information; the static argument above is complete on its own. Behavioural closure if the owner wants it: make the two files share ONE predicate exported from a `src/lib/` module (importable from both — the ESLint ban is on `@/app/**` leaves, not on `src/lib`), so there is one pattern instead of two. P2, unchanged from RT-1149-F3's severity: a latent drift risk over a UI affordance, not a defect at HEAD — at HEAD the two patterns are byte-identical (rt2-1149-13, re-confirmed by r3-01's diff, which shows the single differing line).
